external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app or a self-service kiosk to borrow, renew, reserve, or return books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: The sources do not state how members are authenticated.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who use the circulation page to change loan and member-account records.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand
external_entities.notes: Everyone at the desk uses one shared login; the sources do not identify individual staff members or branches from the recorded action.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: The app on a member's phone that submits borrowing, renewal, and reservation requests to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where a member scans their library card and books being borrowed or returned, and which sends loan and return records to the lending API.
processes.source_excerpt: The kiosks are in every branch and they send each loan and each return to the lending API as it is scanned.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API that receives app, kiosk, and desk requests, checks loan rules, and reads or writes the loans database.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out.
processes.notes: The API's authentication behavior is uncertain. Priya said: "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look." She also said: "Honestly I could not tell you today what it accepts, or what it does with a call it does not like."

processes.name: circulation page
processes.description: The page served by the lending API through which desk staff extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books as returned.
processes.source_excerpt: someone at the desk opens the circulation page and marks it returned, or clears the block on the account
processes.notes: The page is served by the lending API; the source does not establish it as a separately running component.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses, and borrowing history.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: The earlier two-database arrangement was corrected in the interview: the databases were merged into one, and the old reservations database is gone.

data_flows.name: submit loan request
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to borrow, renew, or reserve a book.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
data_flows.data_description: Member and book information for a borrowing, renewal, or reservation request.

data_flows.name: write loan change
data_flows.description: The library app submits a borrowing, renewal, or reservation request to the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.data_description: The specified book or title and member information for a loan, renewal, or reservation.

data_flows.name: scan loan items
data_flows.description: A member scans their library card and books at a self-service kiosk.
data_flows.source_excerpt: a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning
data_flows.data_description: A library card and books being borrowed or returned.

data_flows.name: send loan records
data_flows.description: A kiosk sends each loan and return to the lending API as it is scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether kiosks communicate directly with the loans database.
data_flows.data_description: Loan and return records, including the scanned library card and books.

data_flows.name: change loan records
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page to extend loans, clear account blocks, and mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: The circulation page uses a shared desk login. The source does not identify a separate flow from the page to the lending API because the page is described as being served by the API.

data_flows.name: read and write records
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes member, loan, and reservation records in the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations, and borrowing history.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch self-service kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data centre where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network over which phones reach the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data.
assumptions.basis: The database contains names, email addresses, home addresses, and members' full borrowing history, which are personal data.
